history.notes:
Sensitivity, read and written. The CLIP v2 motion service carries `sensitivity: {status, sensitivity, sensitivity_max}` — re-confirmed for this release against the OpenHue OpenAPI mirror (`src/motion/schemas/MotionGet.yaml`, `MotionPut.yaml`) and aiohue's `MotionSensingFeatureSensitivity` / `MotionSensingFeatureSensitivityPut`, since Signify's own reference for the resource is behind a developer login. The driver publishes `SENSITIVITY` and `SENSITIVITY_MAX` plus a **Motion Sensitivity** property reading `2 of 4`, adopted silently on a read or an eventstream frame like every other reading — including when the Hue app is what changed it. · Sensitivity fires no event, deliberately. It is a configuration value on the sensor, not something that happened in the room, so there is nothing for Composer to trigger on; the variables and the property carry it. · New command **Set Sensitivity** writes the dealer's **Sensitivity** property to the motion service as `PUT {"sensitivity":{"sensitivity":N}}` — the only writable field of that block; `status` and `sensitivity_max` are read-only. It re-checks `LicenseGate()` at the moment of the wire write, rides the same LAN-guarded chokepoint as everything else, and refuses locally and BY NAME — costing zero requests — when nothing is bound, when the motion service id is not known yet, when the sensor has not reported `sensitivity_max`, and when the value is not a finite number or falls outside `0..sensitivity_max`. · An unknown ceiling is refused, not guessed. The popular Python client defaults `sensitivity_max` to 10 in its own model; a driver that inherited that default would cheerfully PUT a 7 to a 4-step sensor. If the accessory has not stated its range, Set Sensitivity says so and sends nothing — and an accessory that never states one does not expose sensitivity at all. · Out of range is refused rather than clamped, which is a deliberate departure from the fleet's clamp-a-dealer-range habit: this ceiling belongs to the DEVICE, so quietly rewriting a 7 into a 4 would report success for a setting the sensor never received. `0` is a real sensitivity (least sensitive) and goes out unchanged. `tonumber("nan")` succeeds and defeats every range test because all comparisons against nan are false, so the numeric reader is non-finite hardened (LAW 1) — the driver will not ship `{"sensitivity":{"sensitivity":nan}}`, which is not JSON. · A successful PUT publishes NOTHING. A 2xx means the bridge accepted the request, not that the sensor is now at N — the read-back (or the stream echo) is the only thing that moves `SENSITIVITY`, exactly as the `enabled` flag already worked. The bridge's own `status: "changing"` is its admission that acceptance is not arrival. · Room-aware discovery. **Discover Sensors** now reads `GET /clip/v2/resource/room` once through the same chokepoint and resolves each device through the rooms' `children` lists, so the listing reads `1. Hallway sensor [Hue motion sensor]  (Hallway)  device 0a1b…`. A device the bridge has in no room — or a room collection that could not be read — prints `(no room)`; no location is ever inferred. The bound sensor's room is annotated onto **Sensor Status** and **Print Configuration** once the bridge has been asked, and a resolved "no room" is remembered so the driver stops asking, while a FAILED room read stays unknown and is asked again on the next heartbeat. · Rooms are decoration and nothing else. Matching, binding, and every state decision stay keyed on the resource id, so a renamed, deleted, or unreadable room changes what a dealer reads and nothing the driver does. · **The parser was rebuilt, and it fixes a defect 0.1.0 shipped.** A real bridge serializes object keys ALPHABETICALLY, which puts `enabled` before a motion service's own `id` and a room's `children` before the room's `id`. 0.1.0 indexed every `"id"` and sliced the bytes to the next one, so on real hardware it never read the `enabled` flag at all — `MOTION_ENABLED` and the Sensing Enabled/Disabled events were dead in the field, and in a multi-sensor collection each resource would have taken its neighbour's flag. Its id-first test fixtures hid the whole class, exactly as they did on the Hue Bridge driver before 0.1.1 (de22cc8). This release cuts REAL object spans out of each `data` array — the string-aware scanner from `integrateit_hue_button` (LAW 2), so a sensor called `Hallway [main` or a room called `Loft ]2[` cannot truncate an enumeration — and every field is read off its own object. Rewriting the fixtures in the bridge's real key order made 3 checks in unmodified 0.1.0 cases fail against the 0.1.0 body; the committed 0.1.0 suite passes unchanged against this one (393 checks, 0 fails). · The `services` array is now walked structurally when deciding whether a device publishes a `motion` service, so an accessory whose customer-typed NAME contains `","rtype":"motion"` can no longer advertise a service it does not have. `*_report` and deprecated-flat payload shapes are still both read for motion, light level, and temperature; a motion resource that omits the `motion` block entirely (which aiohue documents on some firmware) still reads as "no reading in this update" rather than as a value. · `intProp` is non-finite hardened to the fleet's canonical shape (LAW 1). 0.1.0's reader returned a nan unchanged through its own clamp, which could have poisoned the resync timer. · **The eventstream framing was hardened, and a CRLF bridge would have gone silently deaf.** SSE terminates a line with CRLF, LF, or a bare CR, and a bridge (or any proxy in between) that uses CRLF puts `

` between frames — which contains no `

` at all, so the 0.1.0 splitter never completed a single frame on such a peer: no motion, no events, buffer growing until the bound tripped, and the resync heartbeat as the only feedback left. Line endings are now normalized on ingest, with a dangling CR HELD across a chunk boundary so a split inside one terminator cannot fabricate a blank line and cut a frame in half. The held CR is cleared with the buffer whenever a stream opens, so nothing from a retired transfer leaks into its replacement. · The 64KB buffer bound now drops the unterminated residue WHOLE instead of keeping a 4KB tail. The tail was worse than the overflow: it prefixed the next real frame's `data:` line, so the `data:` was no longer at the start of a line and the whole following frame was silently discarded. The bound is stated honestly in the code — any frame whose first 64KB arrive without a terminator is lost, not deferred, and a CLIP v2 envelope is orders of magnitude smaller than that. · Non-finite hardening extended to the READ side and to the PUBLISH side (LAW 1). `%d+` matches a 400-digit integer and `tonumber` overflows it to `inf`, and an `inf` ceiling defeats every range test exactly as `nan` does — it would have made the gate the whole sensitivity feature turns on accept ANY value — so a payload number is not a number until it is finite, and an unrepresentable one is treated as an absent field. The guard on the parse alone was not enough, because both published measurements are CONVERSIONS: lux is exponential in `light_level`, so a finite seven-digit reading (`9999999`) came out of `10 ^ ((raw - 1) / 10000)` as `inf`, and the Fahrenheit conversion multiplies a Celsius value across the same edge. Both refuse at the point the non-finite is manufactured — the bridge's raw value still stands, the derived measurement is simply not published, and no Control4 variable ever carries the string `inf`. **Motion Sensitivity** reads `2 (ceiling Unknown)` when the ceiling is unknowable, never `2 of ?`. · Unchanged on purpose: the baseline-silence rule, the one-shot blind-gap token and its motion-feed scoping, the stream-loss staleness contract, the single-eventstream generation discipline, the LAN guard at the one chokepoint, the TLS trust model, the no-CONTACT_SENSOR decision, and every §8.2 scope statement. Sensitivity can neither consume nor arm the gap token — a case pins that — and the 0.1.0 suite is the regression proof. · Still `releaseStatus: release-candidate` / `hardwareStatus: simulation-verified`: verified against the Control4 API simulator (525 runtime checks, 0 fails, 0 violations), not on a physical bridge, sensor, or controller.

Initial release candidate: local Control4 feedback from one Philips Hue motion accessory over the on-bridge CLIP API v2 (HTTPS, developers.meethue.com). Clean-room original engineering; the pairing, transport, TLS posture, LAN guard, eventstream framing, and reconnect backoff are ported from the shipped IntegrateIT Hue Bridge driver rather than reinvented. · Scope stated in the manifest, the driver header, Start here, the trust section, and Print Configuration: this is a LIGHTING AND COMFORT driver, NOT a security, surveillance, or intrusion device, and not a listed alarm path. Philips Hue Developer Terms §8.2 forbid security/surveillance use of the Hue API, and a battery accessory on a consumer mesh cannot carry a life-safety decision. Never bind it into a security partition. · Link-button pairing built in: Pair (Link Button) POSTs `/api` with `generateclientkey`, handles the error-101 "press the button" round-trip, and stores the returned application key in the password-typed property — never printed, never logged (it rides only in the `hue-application-key` header). · Discover Sensors reads `GET /clip/v2/resource/device` and lists only devices whose service list contains a `motion` service, numbered; Bind Selected Sensor binds the chosen entry into the persisted `Sensor Device` property. Clear Binding and any rebind reset every reading to unknown and fire nothing — no observation has been made against the new id yet. · The bound sensor's four services (motion, light_level, temperature, device_power) are matched two independent ways — the resource names the bound device as its `owner`, or its id is one already learned on a resync — so another sensor's services, a light, a scene, or the SSE envelope's own event id can never move this instance's state. · Push feedback: consumes the /eventstream/clip/v2 SSE stream and publishes MOTION, CONTACT_STATE (OPENED / CLOSED / UNKNOWN, the verified Control4 contact vocabulary), MOTION_ENABLED, LIGHT_LEVEL, LIGHT_LEVEL_RAW, TEMPERATURE, BATTERY_LEVEL, BATTERY_STATE, LAST_MOTION (the bridge's own `creationtime`), STATE_STALE, and BRIDGE_ONLINE; fires Motion Detected/Cleared, Sensing Enabled/Disabled, Battery Low, Bridge Online/Offline, Event Stream Reconnected, and Sensor State Stale. SSE parsing tolerates arbitrary chunk boundaries and keep-alive comments. · Light level is converted honestly: CLIP reports `10000*log10(lux)+1`, the driver inverts it to `lux = 10 ^ ((light_level - 1) / 10000)` and publishes the raw value alongside so the conversion is auditable. A reported 0 sits below the formula's meaningful floor (inverting it yields 0.9998 lux), so the driver publishes 0 lux rather than round that up to 1. Both the flat CLIP fields and the newer `*_report` shapes are read for motion, light level, and temperature. Temperature converts C→F unless Temperature Units says otherwise, and is documented as an in-housing trend signal, not a thermostat reference. · Baseline silence where it belongs, and nowhere else. The first motion reading, the first enabled-flag reading, and the ONE catch-up read after a blind gap all adopt without firing a transition. What the eventstream delivers once it is back does fire: the driver sends no `If-None-Match`, so the bridge replays nothing and a frame arriving on a live stream is a change happening now — including the very first frame after a reconnect, which is usually the walk-past the dealer cares about. The gap token is one-shot and scoped to the motion feed, so a build running on the resync heartbeat alone resumes firing as soon as it has a good read, and a failed battery read never suppresses a motion transition the driver did watch. Battery Low is the deliberate exception in the other direction — a low battery is a standing condition, not a transition, so it reports the first time it is seen and latches until the level recovers. · Stream-loss honesty: a dropped eventstream — or a resync that gets no answer, which is the only signal a build without streaming has — publishes BRIDGE_ONLINE false, fires Bridge Offline and Sensor State Stale, raises STATE_STALE, and relabels Motion State `Stale (feed down) — last seen …`. The last observed values stay published because they are the last thing that was actually true — labelled, never frozen and presented as live, and never replaced by an invented zero. The documented trade is that a change during the blind gap moves the variables but fires no event. · One eventstream at a time. Connect runs on every relevant property change and on every rebind, so the driver refuses to stack a second long-lived transfer on a healthy one. A C4:url() transfer cannot be aborted, so a stream that has been deliberately replaced (Reconnect Event Stream, a rebind, a new bridge address) stays on the wire until the bridge closes it — it carries the generation it was opened under and is ignored from the moment it is replaced, so an abandoned transfer can neither re-apply state nor announce an outage over the stream that took over. Teardown retires the generation for the same reason: a socket closing a minute after OnDriverDestroyed cannot re-arm the reconnect timer. · Enable Sensing / Disable Sensing (PUT the motion service `enabled` flag) is the ONLY writable surface, and both re-check LicenseGate() at wire-write time. Neither fires Sensing Enabled/Disabled — the read-back does, which also means the events fire when someone flips the sensor in the Hue app. A write before any successful read refuses locally, by name, with the fix ("Motion service id unknown — run Resync Now first"). · LAN guard at the ONE transport chokepoint, ahead of header assembly, so the resync, the device read, the pairing claim, the eventstream, and the two writes are all covered — including the boot-time reads, which is the exact path a prior driver leaked an application key through. A blocked host produces zero requests of any kind; the runtime suite asserts the request count against the blocked address is 0 after boot and after every command and action. · Honest TLS trust model: the bridge is self-signed, so the driver connects over HTTPS with CA verification disabled and pins trust to the LAN address + application key; a broken TLS handshake fails closed and never downgrades to plaintext. A single bounded retry honors 429 Retry-After (no retry storm), and stream reconnects use bounded backoff (5s → 60s cap). · No bindable Control4 CONTACT_SENSOR connection, deliberately. Producer-side contact delivery — this driver pushing OPENED/CLOSED to a bound consumer — is unverified SDK surface (still fenced as unverified in the contact-relay template, and shipped by no IntegrateIT driver), and a binding that looks wired while delivering nothing is worse than no binding. Motion reaches Composer as variables and events instead, with CONTACT_STATE carrying the same vocabulary; the runtime suite pins this structurally by failing if a proxy or a CONTACT_SENSOR connection ever appears in the rendered driver.xml. · Known limits: one sensor per instance; sensitivity, outdoor daylight thresholds, and Hue-app automations are not exposed; light level is a conversion rather than a calibrated measurement; temperature reads warm because the sensor sits inside the housing; a change during a stream gap moves the variables but fires no event. · Verified against the Control4 API simulator only — `releaseStatus: release-candidate`, `hardwareStatus: simulation-verified`. Acceptance on a physical Hue Bridge, a physical motion accessory, and a physical controller is not attached to this release.
